title: El Vecino Cocina neighborhood-taqueria campaign: neutralize an 8-dish two-session batch to one house white point, author the paid-social hero set, and data-merge per-special counter cards
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a family-owned, authentic Mexican restaurant in West Palm Beach, FL that wanted static paid-social ad creative for two recurring offers (a Taco Tuesday push and a weekday Lunch Special), with a stated brand personality of 'authentic, community-focused, family-oriented, warm, bold, local neighborhood favorite' and an explicit 'NOT a corporate chain' direction; the real posting named the restaurant, so the brand is laundered to the FICTIONAL 'El Vecino Cocina' (no real company or trademark match) and the ad-network names are genericized to the placements they describe (square feed, portrait feed, vertical story) rather than any social-platform brand. The original literal ask — 'design 12 finished static ad layouts' — mixes generative image work and free-form typesetting/composition the Adobe connector cannot do headlessly, so this benchmark is scoped to the photo-asset-preparation-and-typeset pipeline a production designer genuinely owns: color-managing the client's raw dish photography, authoring the campaign hero look, and typesetting the printed per-special counter cards the taqueria puts on its tables to drive the same promotions. ENRICHMENT (needed to make the chain concrete, failable and measurable): the restaurant photographed EIGHT signature items across TWO service sessions under deliberately different mixed light (a warm tungsten dinner service and a cool prep-kitchen daylight setup), and on the edge of the board in every frame the shooter left a neutral 18% grey reference card (standard practice) so white balance can be reconciled after the fact; the client also supplies a flat scanned wordmark, an authored single-record InDesign counter-card template carrying live merge fields plus two @-prefixed image columns, and a specials roster CSV. The eight-dish count, the two-session lighting split, the in-frame grey card, the per-dish casts, the counter-card deliverable, and the placement ratios are reasonable enrichments consistent with the brief; nothing contradicts the source and no unrelated deliverable was invented.
one_line_ask: Color-manage El Vecino Cocina's eight raw dish photos (shot across two mismatched-light service sessions, each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card) so the whole set neutralizes to one shared house white point, carry a single agent-authored warm-bold neighborhood look across all of them while holding each dish's genuine color true, author the campaign hero into a subject-pop and a color-splash variant plus three paid-social placement ratios, cut one dish onto a clean floating ground, vectorize the scanned wordmark, and data-merge the client's authored counter-card template into one press-ready per-special card set.
full_brief:
You are the production designer prepping the photography and brand assets for El Vecino Cocina, a family-owned, authentic neighborhood taqueria running a paid-social campaign for two recurring offers (a Taco Tuesday push and a weekday Lunch Special). The brand is warm, bold, family-oriented and community-focused, a local favorite and explicitly NOT a corporate chain, and everything has to look appetizing and genuine, never glossy or generic.

Here is the situation with the photos. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you eight raw dish photos of our signature plates, and they do not match out of the folder: they were shot over two service sessions on different days under different light, so straight from the card some run warm and some run cool, a few are a little bright or a little dark, and a couple of the frames came in slightly tilted from being shot by hand. Because we knew the light was inconsistent, we set a neutral 18% grey reference card on the board in every single frame. Your first and most important job is to make the whole set read as ONE kitchen: use the grey card in each frame as your ground truth and correct every photo so that its card reads truly neutral (no leftover warm, cool or green cast) and so the set lands at one shared, consistent brightness and white point. Because the frames start from different light, each one needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to reach that shared target; a single correction copied across all eight will not match, and a set that was each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will not agree at the grey card and we will reject it. One warning from our last freelancer's mistakes: some of our dishes are genuinely deep-colored on purpose (a dark mole, a rich red birria consomme) and were shot under good light, so do not go chasing a cast that is not there and wash out the real color we are selling. When you are done, hand back, per photo, the final white-balance and exposure move you made, so we can confirm the set was matched to the card and not eyeballed.

Second, carry ONE deliberately-designed house look across the whole set on top of the neutralization: a warm, bold, neighborhood-taqueria grade with a little contrast and clarity where the salsa reds and lime greens come forward and the food looks fresh and inviting, applied consistently so every plate feels like the same restaurant. Build that look yourself from real adjustments; do not just click a canned filter.

Third, from the hero al-pastor platter, author the campaign hero: a version where the platter itself is made to stand forward off the table as a scroll-stopping subject, and a separate 'color-splash' version where the food keeps its full color and everything around it falls to muted grey. Then cut the hero into the three placement shapes the campaign needs, keeping the food in frame and using the surrounding table as reframe margin: a square feed, a portrait feed, and a tall vertical story. Keep the reference card out of these finished shapes.

Fourth, cut our carne-asada lunch plate cleanly off its busy table so the dish can float on a solid on-brand ground the layout can drop onto any card.

Fifth, our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper and it came in slightly crooked with a paper margin around it; get it clean, straight and razor-sharp as scalable vector art so it prints crisp at any size.

Finally, build our in-store cards: we have hand-built the InDesign counter-card template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the dish photo, one for the wordmark at the top), and we are giving you the specials roster; merge them so every special gets its own single card with its copy bound and its matching graded dish photo and the crisp wordmark dropped in, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every special, one card per special. Bind our copy and prices verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite them.

Deliverables: the eight matched, house-graded dish masters (as a set our marketing lead can eyeball against the card) plus the per-card product crops; the hero subject-pop and color-splash variants; the hero in square feed, portrait feed and vertical story shapes; the floating carne-asada cutout; the vectorized wordmark; the merged per-special counter-card PDF; and a short sheet listing the white-balance and exposure move you made on each photo.

inputs.name: hero_al_pastor_platter.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid slightly-overhead handheld restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched DSLR look, ~4000x2667 (3:2, full camera resolution), of a generous al pastor taco platter on a rustic wooden table at a family taqueria: three corn tortilla tacos piled with marinated pork, diced onion, cilantro, charred pineapple, lime wedges, a small stone molcajete of bright red salsa, glossy meat catching warm light. Shot under WARM tungsten dinner-service light (~3200K, strong amber cast), slightly flat contrast, and the frame is tilted about 4 degrees from a handheld grab. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a small white chip sits flat on the table at the far LEFT edge of the frame. Real food texture, visible steam, real grease sheen, minor crumbs, documentary realism, no CGI gloss, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: The campaign HERO and the frame that establishes the shared house look. Session A (warm tungsten). Deliberately tilted ~4deg so straightening has work, warm amber cast + slightly flat so a real WB-cool + tone move is needed to land its grey card neutral, and the grey card sits at FAR LEFT so it can be neutralized first and then cropped out when the platter is framed for the placement ratios. Its bright salsa red and lime green are the anchor hues the masked authored pop brings forward. Real specular sheen on the meat means highlights must be protected. ~4000px camera scale so every placement crop (down to 1080-wide) and the ~1500px card crop are honest downscales, never upscales.

inputs.name: carne_asada_lunch_plate.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of a carne asada lunch plate on a plain off-white plate against a moderately busy real table background (other plates, condiments, blurred): grilled sliced steak, rice, refried beans, a folded warm tortilla, pico de gallo, lime. Clear subject/background separation so the dish can be cleanly isolated. Shot under COOL prep-kitchen daylight (~5500K, distinct blue-cool cast), level frame, real char marks and steam. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip rests at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI sheen, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session B (cool daylight), level. The lunch-special hero and the floating-cutout source. Cool/blue cast is the OPPOSITE corrective direction to the warm Session-A frames, so a single shared white balance across the batch cannot neutralize both. Its busy real-table background is a genuine non-trivial edge for the background knockout; the plate is an open dish on a table (outer background only, no enclosed interior hole to punch) so image_remove_background onto a solid ground is the correct, connector-legal cutout path.

inputs.name: birria_tacos_consomme.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of birria tacos beside a small bowl of deep red-brown consomme with chopped onion and cilantro, on a dark ceramic plate on a wood table. Shot under WARM tungsten dinner light (~3200K, amber cast), level frame, real crisp-fried tortilla edges and glistening consomme surface. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip is visible at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session A (warm). RESTRAINT / true-color case: the consomme is a genuinely deep red-brown by nature and was shot under warm light, so after cooling the amber cast to its grey card the correct move HOLDS the rich red rather than desaturating or hue-shifting it toward a 'corrected' brown. The house pop must not push this already-saturated red until it clips. Distinguishing a real deep color from a cast is the reasoning being tested.

inputs.name: chips_guac_salsa.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of a basket of tortilla chips with a bowl of fresh green guacamole and a bowl of bright red salsa on a rustic wood table with a woven textile runner. Shot under COOL prep-kitchen daylight (~5600K, blue-cool cast), and the frame is tilted about 3 degrees. Real chip texture, real avocado and tomato flesh, soft blur behind. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip sits at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session B (cool), tilted ~3deg. Two-hue color-critical frame: the guacamole green and salsa red are both signature brand hues, so after warming its cool cast to neutral against the card, the masked authored pop brings guac-green and salsa-red to the same house pop target used on the hero. The cool cast tends to mute the green; the correction warms and lifts it without turning it acid.

inputs.name: mole_enchiladas.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of enchiladas under a thick, glossy, genuinely dark red-brown mole sauce with sesame seeds and crema drizzle and crumbled queso, on a warm-toned plate on a wood table. Shot under clean NEUTRAL balanced light (~5000K, essentially no color cast), level frame, normal exposure, real sauce sheen and crumb texture. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip sits at the frame edge, and it already reads visually neutral in the raw. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. Shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral and the correct white-balance move is essentially NONE (only match exposure/brightness to the shared set). The mole is a deep red-brown by nature, not because of a cast. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool frames' or 'cool the warm frames' correction it used elsewhere, or that invents a cast to chase, will push this card off-neutral and strip the real color of the dish the client is selling. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not by the batch.

inputs.name: elote_street_corn.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of elote street corn on the cob coated in crema, cotija cheese, chili powder and lime, on a paper-lined tray. Shot under WARM tungsten light (~3200K, amber cast) and slightly OVER-exposed so the crema and cheese verge on blowing out; the frame is tilted about 3 degrees. Real charred kernels, crumbly cheese, dusting of red chili powder. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip sits at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session A (warm), tilted ~3deg, and OVER-exposed. Needs cooling to its grey card AND a downward exposure pull to recover the blown crema/cheese and reach the shared brightness, so both its WB and its tonal move differ from the warm-but-normal birria frame. Its yellow corn and red chili are secondary pop hues brought to the house target by the masked pass; the over-exposure means highlight protection matters here more than anywhere.

inputs.name: margarita_chips_table.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid table scene, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of a salt-rimmed margarita with a lime wheel, condensation on the glass, beside a basket of tortilla chips and a small bowl of red salsa on a rustic wood table with a woven runner. Shot under COOL prep-kitchen daylight (~5600K, blue-cool cast), level frame, real glass refraction and condensation. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip sits at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session B (cool), level. The drink/ambiance scene, previously a declared-but-unused asset in the old spec and now fully consumed as a graded master and a counter-card image. Cool cast warmed to the card like the other Session-B frames but with its own exposure, and its condensation/glass speculars must not clip when it reaches the shared brightness. Two cool frames (this and the chips/guac) still take close-but-not-identical corrections because their light differs.

inputs.name: flan_dessert.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal restaurant photograph, raw un-retouched look, ~4000x2667 (3:2), of a caramel flan on a small plate with a caramel pool and a mint sprig, on a wood table. Shot under a WARM amber lamp (~3000K, strong warm cast) and slightly UNDER-exposed so the shadows go muddy; level frame. Real custard sheen and caramel gloss. A neutral 18% grey reference card with a white chip sits at the frame edge. Documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Session A (warm), UNDER-exposed. Needs cooling to its grey card AND an exposure LIFT (with shadow recovery) to reach the shared brightness, the opposite tonal direction to the over-exposed elote, proving the batch cannot share one exposure move any more than one white balance. The warm caramel is a genuine near-warm color, so the cooling must land the grey card neutral without draining the caramel to grey.

inputs.name: el_vecino_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'El Vecino Cocina' wordmark inked on slightly warm off-white textured paper: a bold hand-lettered wordmark with a small simple emblem (a stylized sombrero over a chili pepper), in flat solid terracotta-red and deep green ink, no gradients. Rendered as a real scan: the off-white paper is NOT transparent and NOT pure white, the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No photographic gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2deg skew, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize fed the raw scan would trace the paper rectangle and bake in the skew, forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/contrast so the flat ink separates hard from the ground, crop to the mark's tight bounds, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Flat solid two-color ink with clean shapes is exactly what traces to a tidy SVG. This mark carries no enclosed-counter knockout claim on a dark ground; it is vectorized on a light ground where counters read correctly.

inputs.name: elvecino_counter_card.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign SINGLE-RECORD counter-card template (.indd/.idml), US Letter portrait for an in-store table card, ONE special per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<special_name>>, <<dish>>, <<offer_line>>, <<when>>, and <<price>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a hero dish-photo frame bound to @DishImage (that row's matching graded dish crop) and a masthead frame at the top bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one special's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @-image-path columns and produces ONE FILE PER ROW, so a single-record counter card is the correct connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. TWO image columns (@DishImage, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row: the row's graded dish crop AND the shared vectorized wordmark, giving the chain-produced wordmark a real connector-doable path onto every card as a merge bind rather than banned free-form placement (mirrors the AO-74 two-image-column pattern).

inputs.name: elvecino_specials_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns special_name,dish,offer_line,when,price,@DishImage,@Wordmark holding 8 rows, one per special: (1) Taco Tuesday Al Pastor; (2) Carne Asada Lunch Plate; (3) Birria Tacos & Consomme; (4) Chips & House Guacamole; (5) Mole Enchiladas; (6) Elote Street Corn; (7) House Margarita; (8) Cinnamon-Caramel Flan. Each row carries a short warm neighborhood offer line, the day or meal it runs (e.g. 'Every Tuesday', 'Weekday lunch 11-3'), and a US-dollar price (e.g. '$3 each', '$11.95'). The @DishImage column names that special's matching graded dish crop file (e.g. @alpastor_card_img.jpg, @carne_card_img.jpg) and the @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file (@logo_vector.svg) in EVERY row. Column names must exactly match the template fields <<special_name>>,<<dish>>,<<offer_line>>,<<when>>,<<price>> and the two @-image-path columns @DishImage and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row merge binds copy, the correct dish photo, AND the shared wordmark per special. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every card via the merge. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight cards; @DishImage points at the eight product-framed crops the chain produces, so every graded dish is consumed (no declared-but-unused asset).

outputs.name: graded_dish_masters_x8
outputs.spec: The eight dish photos brought to one matched house look, delivered in two coupled forms: (a) the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized+graded full-res masters (the *_neutral / *_house frames, each with its in-frame 18% grey card still present), which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts; and (b) the eight product-framed card crops (*_card_img, grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the counter cards. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (1) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing master of each frame, where the grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance, no residual warm/cool/green cast) with the whole set matched to one shared white point and one shared brightness, while every dish's genuine color stays true (no real deep color washed off chasing an absent cast); (2) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered product-framed crop (no grey-card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by the per-image white-balance and exposure report. A single shared correction applied to all eight, or a per-image auto-fix, will diverge at the grey cards and fail claim (1).

outputs.name: hero_subject_pop.jpg
outputs.spec: The al-pastor hero after the shared neutralization + authored house look, with a masked, subject-only lift (select_subject -> masked image_apply_adjustments: local clarity/exposure/contrast on the platter only) so the food reads forward off the table as a scroll-stopping subject WITHOUT lifting or altering the surround. Full-res sRGB JPEG. Built from primitives, not a preset.

outputs.name: hero_color_splash.jpg
outputs.spec: Second hero variant: the food keeps full color while everything around it is dropped to muted grey, produced by inverting the hero subject mask and driving saturation down on the inverted (background) selection only. Full-res sRGB JPEG. A masked selective edit, not a whole-image tint.

outputs.name: hero_placement_set
outputs.spec: The finished subject-pop hero reframed into three paid-social placement shapes by honest crop/downscale of existing pixels (no pixels invented, no canvas extend, no upscale): square feed 1080x1080, portrait feed 1080x1350, and tall vertical story 1080x1920 (the 9:16 cut taken from the full-res popped hero so 1080 width is a downscale, never an upscale). Food kept in frame, surrounding table used as reframe margin, and the far-left grey reference card cropped OUT of all three.

outputs.name: carne_asada_cutout.png
outputs.spec: The neutralized+graded carne-asada lunch plate cleanly isolated off its busy table onto a solid on-brand ground via image_remove_background with a flat backgroundColor (the connector-legal knockout path; the plate is an open dish so only the outer background is removed, no enclosed interior hole is punched), so the dish can float on any card. Grey card removed with the background. Not a select->invert->fill plate.

outputs.name: logo_vector.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the El Vecino Cocina wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark's tight bounds, and knocked to transparency, so it is razor-sharp at any size with no captured paper ground and no skew. Flat two-color mark on a light ground (counters read correctly).

outputs.name: ElVecino_CounterCards_perSpecial.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter portrait counter cards, ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8), exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its special_name/dish/offer_line/when/price verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized graded dish crop dropped into the dish frame (via @DishImage) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark), both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. The Taco Tuesday Al Pastor hero is simply page 1 of this merged set, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (secondary to the images): for each of the eight dish photos, the white-balance move (temperature and tint direction/magnitude) and the exposure move it dialed to land that frame's grey card on the shared white point and brightness, plus a note of the shared house-look constants and any masked HSL pop applied. This makes 'matched to the card' verifiable rather than asserted; the corrections must be NON-identical across the warm and cool frames, and the neutral-light frame must show essentially no white-balance shift.

connector_workflow.note: Level the handheld tilt on the hero platter before any grading or reframing, so the later off-center placement crops are measured against a true horizon. Straightening is applied only to the frames that actually came in tilted; deciding which do is part of the job.

Neutralize the hero to its in-frame 18% grey card so it lands on the shared set white point and brightness, and bake in the shared warm-bold house-look constants (a warm-highlight split, modest contrast, clarity and a gentle vibrance the whole set will carry). Reason the white-balance and exposure from THIS frame's own card and histogram, not from any other frame, and protect the meat speculars from clipping. Authored from adjustment primitives, not a preset and not auto-tone. This full-res frame keeps the grey card in shot and is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading master; report the move for the params sheet.

Semantically select the bright red table salsa and the lime wedges on the platter so the authored color pop is confined to those hues and never touches the grey card, white chip or table. Anchored to named objects, not a hue region or coordinates; returns a maskURI.

Masked, luminosity-preserving HSL confined to the selected salsa/lime: deepen the salsa red within its own red family and lift the lime green's saturation and luminance to the house pop target, letting the existing luminosity carry texture and sheen. A small in-band move (well under a near-complementary rotation), the authored bold look. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image, no mask) and image_fill_area (flat solid fill) would both be wrong here. Establishes the shared house pop target the color-critical dishes are matched to.
Select the platter subject on the graded hero to drive a subject-only lift and, later, the color-splash background. Semantic subject selection; returns a mask.

Masked selective edit: apply a small clarity/exposure/contrast lift to the platter subject ONLY, using the step-5 mask, so the food reads forward off the table while the surround is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit authored from primitives, not a canned 'subject pop' preset. DELIVERABLE hero_subject_pop.jpg and the source for the placement crops.
Invert the platter subject mask so everything BUT the food is selected, for the color-splash background desaturation.

Masked selective edit: drive saturation down on the inverted (background) selection of the graded hero so the food stays full color and the surround falls to muted grey. A masked tonal adjust, not a whole-image tint and not a fill. DELIVERABLE hero_color_splash.jpg.

Honest reframe of the finished hero to a 1080x1080 square feed placement: keep the food in frame, use the table as reframe margin, and crop the far-left grey card OUT. Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only, never a canvas extend or upscale. Part of hero_placement_set.
Honest reframe of the finished hero to a 1080x1350 portrait feed placement, food kept in frame, grey card cropped out. Downscale/reframe only. Part of hero_placement_set.

Honest reframe of the finished hero to a 1080x1920 vertical story placement, cut from the full-res popped hero so the 1080 width is a downscale of the ~1500px-wide vertical strip, never an upscale; food kept in frame, grey card cropped out. Part of hero_placement_set.

Crop the graded hero to the ~1500x1500 product-framed square the counter-card dish frame expects, framing on the platter with the grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only from the ~4000px source so it fills the card frame at ~300 DPI. Binds into the Taco Tuesday Al Pastor card via @DishImage; neutrality is graded on the retained hero_neutral master, never on this crop.

Neutralize the carne-asada lunch plate to its in-frame grey card so it lands on the shared white point and brightness, and apply the shared house-look constants. Reason its WB/exposure from its own card, not from the hero's numbers; hold shadow detail. RETAINED card-bearing master; report the move.

Isolate the plate off its busy table onto a solid on-brand ground via image_remove_background with a flat backgroundColor. The plate is an open dish, so only the outer background is removed (no enclosed interior hole to punch); the grey card leaves with the background. This is the connector-legal knockout; the select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area plate chain is deliberately avoided (fill_area would solid-fill a flat plate and wreck the soft plate/steam edge). DELIVERABLE carne_asada_cutout.png.
Crop the neutralized+graded lunch plate to the ~1500x1500 product-framed square for its counter card, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. Binds into the Carne Asada Lunch card via @DishImage.

Neutralize the birria frame to its in-frame grey card and apply the shared house-look constants, reasoning its WB/exposure from its own card. Keep the deep consomme red true to the dish rather than desaturating or hue-shifting it, and hold it short of clipping under the house pop. RETAINED card-bearing master; report the move.
Crop the neutralized+graded birria to the ~1500x1500 product-framed square, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. Binds into the Birria Tacos card via @DishImage.
Level the tilted chips/guac/salsa frame before grading and cropping.

Neutralize the chips/guac/salsa frame to its in-frame grey card so it lands on the shared white point and brightness, and apply the shared house-look constants, reasoning its WB/exposure from its own card. RETAINED card-bearing master; report the move.

Semantically select the green guacamole and the red salsa so the authored pop is confined to those signature hues and never touches the grey card or the neutral chips. Named objects, not a hue region; returns a mask.

Masked, luminosity-preserving HSL confined to the guac/salsa: bring the guacamole green and the salsa red to the SAME house pop target set on the hero (in-band moves, no near-complementary rotation), so the color-critical dishes read as one restaurant. Existing luminosity carries texture. Cross-asset color match to a common target.
Crop the graded chips/guac/salsa to the ~1500x1500 product-framed square, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. Binds into the Chips & Guacamole card via @DishImage.

Bring the mole enchiladas onto the shared white point and brightness by reading its own in-frame grey card and applying the shared house-look constants. Drive the decision from THIS frame's card and histogram, not from the batch: correct only what its own card shows and hold the dish's genuine color true. RETAINED card-bearing master; report the move (including that white balance was essentially held if the card is already neutral).
Crop the graded mole enchiladas to the ~1500x1500 product-framed square, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. Binds into the Mole Enchiladas card via @DishImage.
Level the tilted elote frame before grading and cropping.

Neutralize the elote frame to its in-frame grey card and reach the shared white point and brightness, applying the shared house-look constants, reasoning its WB and exposure from its own card and histogram; protect the bright crema/cheese highlights while pulling to the set brightness. Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed; straighten it so the vector edges come out square. Tracing the raw skew would bake the rotation into the SVG.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the warm off-white paper toward white so the flat terracotta/green ink separates hard from the ground; a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and emblem only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency on a light ground (counters read correctly), not a select->invert->fill.

Trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card masthead and any scale. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette; this prep chain is what avoids that. DELIVERABLE logo_vector.svg.

difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: 42 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grade/mask/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), well above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the two upload steps and the auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (warm Session-A frames cooled, cool Session-B frames warmed, one over-exposed frame pulled down, one under-exposed frame lifted, one genuinely deep-colored frame held true, one neutral-light frame given essentially no WB shift) all forced to converge on a single measurable target, the in-frame 18% grey card, so a blanket batch correction or a per-image auto-fix cannot pass. Layered on top: an agent-AUTHORED house look built from image_apply_adjustments primitives (a warm split-tone/contrast/clarity constant set) plus masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pops on the color-critical dishes (salsa red, guac green, corn yellow) matched to a shared pop target, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone; a masked subject-only lift on the hero and a masked color-splash both authored from primitives (no canned 'subject pop' preset); a connector-legal floating cutout via image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) rather than select->invert->fill; a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white wordmark scan; and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template as the owned typeset endpoint. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (all crops downscale from ~4000px camera-scale sources), no compositing, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is not used; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only; the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast and the old image_apply_preset 'Subject Pop' are all replaced by image_apply_adjustments and masked primitives. All steps are headless [C] except the authored-template merge [T].
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION the agent can trip, not a self-measurement): every photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance test is that each card, graded on its RETAINED card-bearing master, reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance, no residual warm/cool/green cast) with the whole set matched to one shared white point and brightness while every dish's genuine color stays true; the agent must REPORT the per-image white-balance and exposure move it dialed, so a naive agent that copies one correction across the batch, or per-image auto-fixes each frame, leaves the cool frames blue and the warm frames amber, the cards disagree, and the set fails. Card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the product-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT), so neutrality is never evaluated on a card-removed file. A third gate is the merge: output page-count must equal roster row-count (8), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight frames shot under two opposite casts on differing exposure directions, which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT needs DIFFERENT per-frame corrections; (2) an agent-authored warm-bold house look from primitives plus masked HSL pops matched to one shared salsa-red/lime-green/guac-green target so the color-critical dishes read as one kitchen; plus a masked subject lift and masked color-splash that must not touch the surround, prep-before-trace logo discipline, and the connector-legal knockout path. THE TRAP: the mole enchiladas were shot under near-neutral light so their grey card is already neutral and the mole is a genuinely deep red-brown; the naive path batch-applies the same cast correction used on the other frames (or invents a cast to chase), pushing the card off-neutral and washing out the real color the client sells, while the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. Secondary traps: copying the hero's exact WB onto the opposite-cast frames; running a canned preset/auto-tone as 'the look'; using select->invert->fill for the cutout (bricks the edge); and cropping the grey card out before neutralizing (destroys the reference). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral within tolerance and one shared white point/brightness on all eight RETAINED card-bearing masters, with the neutral-light frame showing essentially no WB shift and no dish's real color drained; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight product-framed crops; (c) hero delivered as subject-pop + color-splash + square 1080x1080 / portrait 1080x1350 / story 1080x1920 placements with the card removed; (d) carne cutout on a solid ground; (e) wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground SVG; (f) exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter card per roster row; plus the per-image WB/exposure report so 'matched to the card' is verifiable rather than asserted.
